description: DSA problems, TCS CodeVita patterns, and company-specific coding questions for placement preparation across TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Deloitte, Accenture, Cognizant, and other top companies.

questions.title: Find the Missing Number
questions.problem: Given an array of n-1 integers in the range [1, n], find the missing number. The array contains all distinct values.
questions.constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4, all elements are unique, one number is missing

approach.brute_force: Sort the array and find where consecutive elements differ by more than 1. Time: O(n log n), Space: O(1)
approach.optimal: Use sum formula. Expected sum = n*(n+1)/2. Missing = Expected sum - Actual sum. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)
approach.xor_approach: XOR all elements with numbers 1 to n. Result will be the missing number. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)

questions.title: Maximum Subarray Sum (Kadane's Algorithm)
questions.problem: Given an integer array, find the contiguous subarray which has the largest sum and return its sum.

approach.optimal: Kadane's Algorithm: Track current sum and max sum. Reset current sum to 0 if it goes negative. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)

questions.solution_python:
def max_subarray(nums):
    max_sum = nums[0]
    curr_sum = nums[0]
    for num in nums[1:]:
        curr_sum = max(num, curr_sum + num)
        max_sum = max(max_sum, curr_sum)
    return max_sum

questions.title: Check if a string is an Anagram
questions.problem: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.
questions.constraints: 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 5*10^4, strings consist of lowercase English letters

approach.optimal: Use a frequency count array of size 26. Increment for s, decrement for t. If all zeros, it's an anagram. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)

questions.title: Reverse Words in a String
questions.problem: Given a string s, reverse the order of words. Words are separated by spaces. The output should not have leading/trailing spaces.

approach.optimal: Split by spaces, filter empty strings, reverse the list, and join. Time: O(n), Space: O(n)

questions.title: Detect a Cycle in a Linked List
questions.problem: Given a linked list, determine if it has a cycle. A cycle occurs when a node's next pointer points back to a previous node.

approach.optimal: Floyd's Cycle Detection (Tortoise and Hare): Use two pointers, slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. If they meet, there's a cycle. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)

questions.title: Reverse a Linked List
questions.problem: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.

approach.iterative: Use three pointers: prev, curr, next. Iterate and reverse links. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)
approach.recursive: Recursively reverse the rest of the list and fix the head link. Time: O(n), Space: O(n) stack

questions.solution_python:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr:
        next_node = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = next_node
    return prev

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.problem: Given a string s containing '(', ')', '{', '}', '[', ']', determine if the input string is valid. An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of bracket and in the correct order.

approach.optimal: Use a stack. Push opening brackets. For closing brackets, check if the top of the stack matches. Time: O(n), Space: O(n)

questions.title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
questions.problem: Given weights and values of n items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity W to get the maximum total value. You cannot break an item.

approach.dp_table: Create a 2D DP table dp[i][w]. For each item, either include or exclude it. Time: O(n*W), Space: O(n*W)

questions.title: Longest Common Subsequence
questions.problem: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. A subsequence is a sequence derived by deleting some or no elements without changing order.

approach.dp_table: Create dp[i][j] = LCS of text1[:i] and text2[:j]. If chars match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]+1. Else max of dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]. Time: O(m*n), Space: O(m*n)

questions.title: Fibonacci Number (Bottom-Up DP)
questions.problem: Given n, return the nth Fibonacci number. F(0)=0, F(1)=1, F(n)=F(n-1)+F(n-2).

approach.memoization: Top-down DP with memo. Time: O(n), Space: O(n)
approach.optimal: Bottom-up with two variables. Time: O(n), Space: O(1)

questions.title: Level Order Traversal (BFS)
questions.problem: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (from left to right, level by level).

approach.optimal: Use a queue (BFS). Process nodes level by level. At each level, record all values, then enqueue children. Time: O(n), Space: O(n)

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.problem: Given a 2D grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), count the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.

approach.dfs: For each unvisited '1', run DFS to mark all connected '1's as visited. Increment island count. Time: O(m*n), Space: O(m*n)

questions.title: Binary Search
questions.problem: Given a sorted array of integers and a target value, return the index if the target is found. Otherwise, return -1.

approach.optimal: Binary search: Use left and right pointers, check mid element. Time: O(log n), Space: O(1)

questions.title: Number Spiral
questions.problem: Generate an n x n matrix filled with numbers 1 to n^2 in a spiral order (clockwise from top-left).

approach.simulation: Simulate the spiral movement using direction vectors. Keep track of boundaries. Time: O(n^2), Space: O(n^2)

questions.solution_python:
def generate_spiral(n):
    matrix = [[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    top, bottom, left, right = 0, n-1, 0, n-1
    num = 1
    while top <= bottom and left <= right:
        for i in range(left, right+1): matrix[top][i] = num; num += 1
        top += 1
        for i in range(top, bottom+1): matrix[i][right] = num; num += 1
        right -= 1
        for i in range(right, left-1, -1): matrix[bottom][i] = num; num += 1
        bottom -= 1
        for i in range(bottom, top-1, -1): matrix[i][left] = num; num += 1
        left += 1
    return matrix

questions.title: Caesar Cipher
questions.problem: Given a string and a shift value, apply Caesar cipher encryption. Uppercase and lowercase letters shift within their case. Non-alphabetic characters remain unchanged.

questions.title: Find Second Highest Salary
questions.problem: Write a SQL query to get the second highest salary from the Employee table.
questions.solution: SELECT MAX(Salary) AS SecondHighestSalary FROM Employee WHERE Salary < (SELECT MAX(Salary) FROM Employee);
questions.alternate_solution: SELECT DISTINCT Salary FROM Employee ORDER BY Salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

questions.title: Find Employees with Salary Above Average
questions.problem: Write a SQL query to find all employees whose salary is above the average salary.
questions.table_schema: Employee(Id INT, Name VARCHAR, Salary INT, Department VARCHAR)
questions.solution: SELECT Name, Salary FROM Employee WHERE Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM Employee) ORDER BY Salary DESC;

questions.title: Department-wise Maximum Salary
questions.problem: Write a SQL query to find the maximum salary in each department.
questions.table_schema: Employee(Id INT, Name VARCHAR, Salary INT, Department VARCHAR)
questions.solution: SELECT Department, MAX(Salary) AS MaxSalary FROM Employee GROUP BY Department ORDER BY MaxSalary DESC;
